notes: §1985:XIV.3.2.3 SR4: "Literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 must be defined as alphanumeric." CommunicationBinder.BindPath asks IsAlphanumericKey of the KEY operand (the phrase reaches only 85; at 2002 and 2023 COBOL0902 removes it) and refuses with COBOL6171; the witness refuses KEY 123. Probes at --std 85: refused, rightly: literals 123, -1, 1.5, N"AB"; PIC 9(4), S9(3)V9, A(4), ZZ9.99, COMP items, a numeric child of a group, FUNCTION LENGTH, K-A(1:2) (alphabetic stays alphabetic); accepted and run (STATUS KEY 20): "PASSWORD", PIC X(10), a group, X(10:1), an OCCURS DEPENDING ON element and its (1:3), SPACE, ZERO, ALL "K", HIGH-VALUES, FUNCTION UPPER-CASE and its (1:3). The defect: a reference-modified numeric or numeric-edited item, which §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5 makes class and category alphanumeric, is refused (K-9(1:2), K-S9(1:2), K-NE(1:3); ENABLE KEY K-9(1:2) the same), because IsAlphanumericKey asks Place.Item, the underlying item, not RefModPlace.Category (the PB70 ref-mod category reader). Open question, not counted: PIC XXBXX (alphanumeric edited) is accepted while ZZ9.99 is refused, consistent with neither the category nor the class reading of "defined as alphanumeric". Degenerate KEY with no operand and KEY twice are parse errors (COBOL0001, COBOL2269). kb/Work PB5384 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read3/rd-10.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Literal-1 or the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 must be defined as alphanumeric."; 2023: "No DISABLE statement or Communication module in 2023; no candidate clause holds the feature". No 2023 clause holds the DISABLE statement. The wording candidates cover CANCEL, CALL, SEND, MOVE and others, not the DISABLE key operand, so the feature is dropped.
